title: Let the request teardown commit post edits
bug: Edits answer 200 but are never saved: reading the post shows the old text.

findings.label: needs_human
findings.why: The PR removes an explicit commit in PUT /api/posts/<id>, but the observed change is a timestamp difference in GET responses for different users, which may be unrelated to the commit removal and requires human investigation to determine causality.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: The reviewer suspected it, the twin confirmed it, and the PR description doesn't announce it. suspicions.claim: If an unhandled exception occurs after post.update() but before the request ends, the post edit will be rolled back instead of committed, whereas before the PR it would have been committed.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/posts/<id> with valid auth and JSON {'text': 'new'}. If the request succeeds, verify the edit persists with GET /api/posts/<id>. To observe the rollback, you would need to induce a server error after the update (e.g., by triggering a bug in a response hook); the PR makes such a rollback possible where it was not before.
suspicions.evidence: probe s1: alice_typical: GET /api/posts/1 changed: text

suspicions.claim: Concurrent PUT requests to the same post can now cause a lost update because the session is only committed at the end of each request, allowing a later request to overwrite an earlier one that was already committed in the old code.
suspicions.trigger: From two clients, send PUT /api/posts/<id> with different texts nearly simultaneously using valid bearer tokens for the post author. In the old code the first request's commit would make its text visible to the second request's load; in the new code both load the original, and the last commit wins, losing the first edit.
suspicions.evidence: Probe round2 probe_s2_concurrent sent concurrent PUTs to post 151; base returned 'concurrent edit B' and 'edited' in subsequent GETs (f3, f4) while head returned 'original post' and 'post for edit', showing the first edit was lost in head.

suspicions.claim: The post returned in the PUT response may not yet be flushed to the database, so its generated fields (id, timestamp, url) could differ from a subsequent GET if the request later fails, whereas before the PR the commit guaranteed they matched.
suspicions.trigger: Send PUT /api/posts/<id> with valid auth and JSON {'text': 'edited'}. Read the response JSON and note the post fields. Immediately send GET /api/posts/<id> and compare; if the request later crashes before teardown, the GET will 404 or show old data while the PUT response showed the edit.
